active.title: [bug] 在会话不显示 MiniMax Code 的会话

new.body:
Windows desktop reproduction, confirming the root cause on current main and adding the moved-data-folder case.

### Environment

- magpie v0.1.4209 (`magpie-windows-amd64.exe`, built 2026-11-15) and the running desktop app v0.1.4966 (started 2026-11-27), Windows 11.
- MiniMax Code desktop (CN build). Its data folder is moved to `D:\minimax data\.minimax` — a path that contains a space — which the app records in its own electron-store file `%APPDATA%\MiniMax\minimax-agent-cn-config.json` as `config.localRuntimeDataParentDir: "D:\\minimax data"` (previous parent: `C:\Users\16439`, whose `~/.minimax` still holds 5,747 pre-move session files).
- Session layout on disk is exactly the documented one: `v2/sessions/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<hh-mm-ss-ms>-session_<base64>/messages.jsonl` (plus `manifest.json`, `history-catalog.json`, `llm-call.json`, `user-message-locators.jsonl`, `reports/`).

### Reproduction (installed binary, non-interactive)

```console
$ magpie sessions --json --limit 5000
# 524 sessions, 10 agents: hermes 208, codex 187, zcode 71, agy 27, cursor 14,
# kimi 10, dsh 4, claude 2, opencode 1 — zero minimax-code

$ magpie usage
#   agents
#   MiniMax Code       56% 1.21B   111577 calls   <- top agent by tokens
#   kimi-code-desktop  16% ...
#   ...

$ magpie sessions read
#   on   MiniMax Code (minimax-code)      <- Found() lists it, consent is on

$ magpie ls
#   MiniMax Code      magpie/stepfun-cn/step-5-preview    D:\minimax data\.minimax\config.yaml
```

So on this machine the data folder resolves correctly (the #2998/#4870 fix works, space in the path included), `Found()` lists `minimax-code`, consent is on — and the Sessions page still has no MiniMax Code rows, while the Usage reader counts MiniMax Code as the busiest agent. The files are found and parsed by one reader and never asked for by the other.

### Isolation (it is not the path, the space, or the moved folder)

- `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR=C:\Users\16439\.minimax` (the old default, 5,747 session files): still zero minimax-code sessions listed.
- A clean-room run with a synthetic `USERPROFILE`/`APPDATA` (no desktop store file), a synthetic `.minimax/v2/sessions/2026/11/27/10-00-00-000-session_<base64>/messages.jsonl` with one assistant message carrying `usage`, and consent pre-set: `magpie sessions read` reports MiniMax Code found and on; `magpie sessions --json` lists zero minimax-code sessions.

### Root cause, on current main

Checked out at e0ed2c4 (2026-11-14); the same gap is present in v0.1.4209 (2026-11-15) and the running v0.1.4966 (2026-11-27), i.e. the fix branch has not landed:

- `minimaxCallFiles()` (`internal/sessions/calls_minimax.go:47`) is referenced from exactly one place: `callSourcesInto` (`internal/sessions/calls.go:347`) — the Usage/calls reader. That is #1605, and it works: the walk, the base64 session id, the messages.jsonl parse.
- `allFilesWith` (`internal/sessions/sessions.go:1001-1010`) — the file list behind the Sessions page (`Manage` → `agentCounts(allFiles())` → the source dropdown, and `List`) — lists every other agent's session files and not MiniMax Code's. There is no `minimaxFiles()` session lister, only the call lister.
- `parserFor` (`internal/sessions/sessions.go:2299`) has no `minimax-code` case, so even a listed file would fall to the default Claude parser.
- `Found()` (`internal/sessions/access.go:248`) does register `minimax-code` (folder existence only), so the consent card shows MiniMax Code as found, the user allows it — and the page still shows nothing. That mismatch is what makes this read as "magpie ignores MiniMax Code" rather than "Usage reads it, Sessions doesn't".

This agrees with skygunner's root cause in this issue and jytx's confirmation on main; what this adds is the Windows desktop evidence, the moved data folder with a space in the path, and the Usage-vs-Sessions split with numbers (top agent by usage, zero sessions listed).

### Minimal fix

Same shape as the branch on this issue: list MiniMax Code's `messages.jsonl` in `allFilesWith` (a `minimaxFiles()` beside `minimaxCallFiles()`, sharing the walk), add a `minimax-code` case to `parserFor` (session id from the folder name's decoded `mvs_…`, which matches the Usage records' `session`), and keep `Deletable` false with the page's existing "list only" note until resume/delete exist.

new.body:
New real-upstream reproduction (2026-11-28) — this fills the "not verified against a real Qoder upstream" gap noted in the previous analysis.

Env: magpie `0.1.4794`, `@magpie-community/opencode-qoder-auth` `0.2.77`, Win11, gateway `127.0.0.1:3425`.

From `~/.config/magpie/usage.jsonl` (qoder-cn, `personal_standard`, 1400/2400 credits left — so not a quota issue):

- At `2026-11-28T08:14:57+08:00`, **15 models returned 503 in the same second**: dfmodel, hmodel, qfmodel, qmodel_38max, qmodel_latest, dmodel, gfmodel, gmodel_latest, gmodel, jmodel, kmodel, kmodel_latest, mmodel, fast (lmodel separately).
- `dfmodel`'s refusal is exactly this issue's wording:

  `Qoder queued the request for dfmodel (this plan's queue: p4, 1 ahead); try again in 60s (the queue hasn't moved in 5 minutes with nothing ahead)`

- The gateway then rested the **whole account**: `{"why":"other","status":503,"by":"backoff","key":"qoder-cn@<uuid>"}` and refused every sibling model without asking upstream — the exact failure mode of #3213, reproduced on a current released build.
- `lmodel` is a separate case: `providers.json` has it `delisted` since 2026-11-11, so its 400 is expected.

Same shape as #6819 (28 probes, all 503 in one second, UI still "all models available"); same error as #7701.

**On the A/B decision:** the live refusal names ONE model ("for `dfmodel`") and carries that model's own queue position. It is model-scoped, not an account-wide outage — which supports **A**: rest `restID` only, keep siblings served. @skygunner's `fix/queue-model-rest` already has `TestQueuedModelRestsAlone` (red before, green after); it needs a rebase since `restAfterMarked` has moved. Not claiming the branch is ready — only that the live evidence points to A, and the maintainer's A-vs-B call is what is blocking a patch. Happy to re-run the branch tests on current main if that helps.

issue.title: gateway: a vendor's image-count cap ends a routing group instead of failing over (Cloudflare: "too many images in request (max 32)")

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
## What happens

A routing group whose first member is Cloudflare Workers AI (DeepSeek) answers a request carrying more than 32 images with

```
400 Cloudflare: AiError: AiError: Invalid data for image - reason too many images in request (max 32) (<uuid>)
```

The group ends there: the second member (official DeepSeek) is never asked, and the client's retry is sent to Cloudflare again, so the turn can never succeed. The routing log holds exactly one try:

```json
{"model":"group/many-deepseeks","status":400,
 "tries":[{"id":"cloudflare","model":"@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017",
           "status":400,"fail":"other",
           "error":"Cloudflare: AiError: AiError: Invalid data for image - reason too many images in request (max 32) (<uuid>)"}],
 "done":true,"served":null}
```

No `rest` on that try, so the next request asks Cloudflare first again.

## Reproduction

1. Group, `routing=order`: `cloudflare/@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` → `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.
2. Send one user message with 33 distinct PNGs (8×8 is enough), Chat Completions or Messages:

```python
content = [{"type": "text", "text": "count"}] + [
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64," + imgs[i]}} for i in range(33)
]
```

Actual: HTTP 400 as above, one try, `fail: "other"`, the second member never asked, the first never rested.
Expected: the second member is asked the same request (as #4732's GLM refusal now does), and the first is not rested.

Controls, same machine, magpie 0.1.3291 / 0.1.3292:

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| 32 distinct images to Cloudflare | 200 |
| 33 distinct images to Cloudflare | 400 (above) |
| one data URL repeated 64 times | 200 — Cloudflare counts distinct images, not occurrences |
| the same 33-image request to `deepseek/deepseek-flash` alone | 200 |

Raw upstream body, asked directly:

```json
{"errors":[{"message":"AiError: AiError: Invalid data for image - reason too many images in request (max 32) (<uuid>)","code":8006}],"success":false,"result":{},"messages":[]}
```

## Why it doesn't fail over

The words match none of the refusal classes `retryable()` reads, so `holdWriter.failed()` is false and the serve loop's two failover branches (the shape branch and the `!last && hw.failed()` branch) are both skipped.

Checked against current main (`0f8c3d867`, v0.1.3315), `internal/gateway/fallback.go`:

- `shapeWords` — no match
- `zhipuImageRefusal` (the only image wording there is, from #4732) — no match
- `quotaWords`, `creditWords`, `unservedWords`, `refusedWords` — no match
- `bodyCapWords` (`body_cap.go`) — no match: it reads a *byte* cap, and `statedCap` only parses `bytes|kb|mb|gb`, never `(max 32)`

`failure()` therefore returns `failOther` and the route ends.

## Suggested direction

This is the same class as #2887, #2313, #3794 and #5374: a refusal that is about the request's shape on this member, which another member serves. The smallest fix is one alternative in `shapeRefused`/`retryable`'s word lists (as #4732 did for GLM and #3794 proposes for Kilo's tool count): the next member is asked once, nobody rests.

The fuller fix is the count analogue of the byte cap already in `internal/gateway/body_cap.go`: `byteCapRefusal` learns the cap, `withinCap`/`refitOverCap` leave the oldest history images out (`withoutOldImages`), and `bodyCaps` remembers it per provider. An image-count cap would compare `len(historyImages(...))` with the number the refusal states, and could be remembered the same way (`unfit` / `bodyCaps`). A vendor capability field would be the cleanest of all, but nothing in `internal/provider` or `internal/catalog` models an image count today.

## Related

- #2887 — the same gap (a vendor 400 not read as channel-missing), fixed by a wording in the list in v0.1.2497
- #4732 — an image refusal already handled as a shape refusal, the closest precedent
- #3794 — a vendor *count* cap (tools, 128) with the identical log shape; patch posted, no reply yet
- #2313, #5374, #4632 — same class, each fixed by one wording
- #1421, #5226 — the configurable error-policy direction (agreed, not built)
- #5194 — learn a per-leg cap from the vendor's own 400
- #4239 — images count 0 in the routing estimate (adjacent, not this)

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.3291 (macOS 27, arm64), gateway `127.0.0.1:3425`; also reproduced through another magpie 0.1.3292 as a `remote-magpie` provider
- Cloudflare Workers AI, model `@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `POST /v1/messages` (translated)
- second member `deepseek/deepseek-flash` (official API), `routing=order`

- **required**：发往 api.x.ai 的工具 schema 里，凡是 `type` 为 `object`（或 type 列表含 `object`）、`required` 为 null 或者没写的节点，都补成 `"required": []`。根、`properties`、`items`/`prefixItems`、`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`、`$defs` 等子 schema 都处理；真正的数组（如 Bash 的 `["command"]`）原样保留；`default`/`enum` 里的数据不动。只重写 `tools` 数组，请求体其余部分逐字节不变。`/v1/messages/count_tokens` 也走同样的处理。
- **stop**：发往 api.x.ai 的 `/v1/messages` 去掉非空的 `stop_sequences`，`/v1/chat/completions` 去掉非空的 `stop`（字符串或数组都算），直通和翻译两条路径都处理。空值原样发出，Responses 不动。auto-mode 分类器少了 `</block>` 这个 stop 之后，Claude Code 照样能解析回复（它的解析器不要求闭合标签）。

issue.title: gateway: xAI's Messages stream may send content_block_delta without index (yangfei1024's 2c9cf0f, unverified)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
In #3392, yangfei1024 (11-07, commit 2c9cf0f on `fix/xai-tools-required-and-stream-index`) reports that xAI's Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` stream sends `content_block_delta` events with no `index`. Only `content_block_start` and `content_block_stop` carry one. A strict client decoder (ZCode named) then fails with `["index"]: expected number, received undefined` and drops the whole turn.

The patch adds `xai_stream_index.go` (`xaiIndexTidy`). It tracks the open block's index in the passthrough SSE path and fills a missing one. The hook is scoped to `p.Host()=="api.x.ai" || grokModel(...)`.

This was not shipped with the #3392 required/stop fix because nothing in the thread shows the bytes:
- There is no captured xAI stream with a delta lacking `index`. The patch's test builds its own.
- guqing and TwinsDestiny, both on Claude Code against api.x.ai, got normal streams once the request was accepted.
- No xAI key is available here to capture one, and real-account probes are off the table.

To take it:
1. Capture a real xAI `/v1/messages` stream that lacks `index`: the raw SSE bytes, and which model and request.
2. Build the test fixture from those bytes, then port 2c9cf0f's `xaiIndexTidy` with credit to yangfei1024.
3. Check the sibling: the same stream translated to Chat or Responses (`forwardTranslated`) reads `index` too.

issue.title: [Bug] Codex compaction fails : input[N].type must be one of ... (custom_tool_call history not translated)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

issue.body:
### magpie version

v0.1.4928 (Settings → About). Checked against main 22f0f3f1aeda02c9cdbf825fab0e68d68cbdf8e9.

### Where

Gateway only

### OS

macOS 26 (Apple Silicon)

### Agent, provider and model

Codex CLI 0.172.0 → magpie (http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1, wire_api = "responses") → hy4-openai/hy4
(x-magpie-provider: hy4-openai)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Let magpie generate ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.codex/magpie-models.json.
   The generated catalog sets `apply_patch_tool_type: "freeform"` for every model,
   including hy4-openai/hy4.
2. Start a Codex session and use `apply_patch` at least once. The rollout then
   contains `custom_tool_call` / `custom_tool_call_output` pairs.
3. Continue until `total_usage_tokens` crosses `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 800000`
   (observed: 800681), or trigger compaction manually.
4. Codex sends a compaction request to POST /v1/responses with the full history.
5. The upstream returns HTTP 400 and the turn fails. Every later turn retries
   pre-sampling compaction and fails with the same error, so the thread is stuck.

### What happened, and what you expected

Observed:

```json
{"id":"<error-id-1>","error":{"message":"hy4-openai: input[261].type must be one of: message, function_call, function_call_output, web_search_call, item_reference, reasoning, tool_search_call, tool_search_output (HTTP 400, invalid_input, request id <request-id-1>)","type":"invalid_input","param":"","code":""}}
```

Second attempt on the same thread:

```json
{"id":"<error-id-2>","error":{"message":"hy4-openai: input[261].type must be one of: message, function_call, function_call_output, web_search_call, item_reference, reasoning, tool_search_call, tool_search_output (HTTP 400, invalid_input, request id <request-id-2>)","type":"invalid_input","param":"","code":""}}
```

The hy4-openai `/responses` input whitelist omits `custom_tool_call` and
`custom_tool_call_output`, although both are valid `input[]` item types in the
OpenAI Responses API. Codex replays them during compaction because the generated
catalog declared apply_patch as a freeform custom tool.

Local evidence:

- Codex rollout log (`~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*`): first unsupported pair is
  response_item #260 `custom_tool_call` (name=apply_patch) and #261
  `custom_tool_call_output`; with the one leading instruction item this maps to
  `input[261]`. A second session showed the same pattern with `input[202]` and
  its first unsupported pair at #201/#202.
- Codex logs database: rows show `run_auto_compact{reason=ContextLimit
  phase=MidTurn}` and `run_pre_sampling_compact → run_auto_compact{... phase=PreTurn}`,
  `token_limit_reached=true`, then `Failed to run pre-sampling compact`.
  Normal `/v1/responses` turns immediately before the failure were 200.
- magpie gateway log contains a similar earlier record:
  `input[202].type must be one of: ... invalid_input ... compact`.

Current main does not classify this response as a retryable input-kind refusal:

- `inputKindWords` (internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:4367) only matches
  `unsupported[ _]input[ _]item|unknown item type`.
- `customToolRefusal` (internal/gateway/custom_tool.go:26) matches
  `unsupported custom tool|custom tools not supported|unknown variant \`custom\`` etc.,
  but this error never names `custom_tool_call`; it only says `must be one of`.
- `shapeWords` (internal/gateway/fallback.go) has no `must be one of` / `invalid_input` alternative.
- `hasCustomTool` (internal/gateway/custom_tool.go:32) early-returns unless the body
  contains the literal `"custom"`; a compaction request has `tools: []` and only
  `custom_tool_call` history items, so it is not detected. This is the same blind
  spot described in #3849, but with a different refusal wording.
- The plain-text compaction fallback added for `unsupported_input_item`
  (#5181 / v0.1.3139) does not fire: this error has `type: "invalid_input"`,
  `param: ""`, and different wording.

Expected: when a provider rejects a Responses `input[]` item with an enum/whitelist
error like `input[N].type must be one of: ...`, magpie should either

1. translate `custom_tool_call` / `custom_tool_call_output` history items into
   `function_call` / `function_call_output` before forwarding to that provider, or
2. classify it as an input-kind refusal and retry compaction via `plainCompact` /
   local summary, as done for #5181 / proposed in #7961,

so the session is not locked on every subsequent turn. It would also help to avoid
generating `apply_patch_tool_type: "freeform"` for providers whose `/responses`
input whitelist excludes custom tool items.

### Related issues (checked, not duplicates)

- #3849 — vLLM `Unsupported input item type: custom_tool_call` during Codex compaction;
  fork fix extends `customToolRefusal` / `hasCustomTool`, but its wording match does
  not cover `input[N].type must be one of: ...`.
- #7961 — Copilot `Invalid value: 'other'. Supported values are ...`; proposes
  extending `inputKindWords` for enum refusals. `must be one of` is another such wording.
- #4149 — Qwen Responses rejects `web_search_call` in compaction history.
- #6150 / #5181 — Command Code `unsupported_input_item`, fixed in v0.1.3139.
- #3831 — custom_tool_call dropped on translated Responses path.

### Error text or logs

```text

status=400
x-magpie-model: hy4-openai/hy4
x-magpie-provider: hy4-openai
x-request-id: <request-id-1>  (12:50:30 UTC)
x-request-id: <request-id-2>  (13:10:03 UTC)

hy4-openai: input[261].type must be one of: message, function_call,
function_call_output, web_search_call, item_reference, reasoning,
tool_search_call, tool_search_output (HTTP 400, invalid_input, request id <request-id>)

```

issue.body:
## 需求描述

MiniMax Code 的会话在 Magpie「会话」页面中没有正常显示对应的用量信息，无法按具体会话查看请求与上下文用量。

## 期望结果

希望「会话」页面能把 MiniMax Code 的会话与对应的用量数据关联起来，并正常展示每个会话的请求数、Token 用量及可用的上下文用量信息。如果某类数据无法从会话记录中取得，也希望界面明确说明支持范围。

## 查看方式

1. 在 MiniMax Code 中产生若干轮对话。
2. 打开 Magpie 的「会话」页面，查看对应的 MiniMax Code 会话及其用量信息。

## 补充

这项需求关注的是**会话页面中的展示与会话关联**，与 #1605 中 MiniMax Code 请求计入 Agent 用量的统计覆盖问题不同。当前未提供 Magpie / MiniMax Code 版本、操作系统及会话页面具体表现截图，后续可补充以便复现。
